body:
### Describe the bug

With `CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE`, importing a module again after removing it from `sys.modules` crashes the process.

What happens:

1. On the second import, `__pyx_pymod_create` gives back the module that already exists ([ModuleSetupCode.c#L1781](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/997aeea7410c0b7e0904efab62553145064f2ff8/Cython/Utility/ModuleSetupCode.c#L1781-L1782)).
2. CPython drops the state of whatever `Py_mod_create` returns and gives it a new, empty one ([moduleobject.c#L361](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/58ed60b7415e218ce3d608302e39b5e55bfb0e88/Objects/moduleobject.c#L361)).
3. The exec function sees the module as already set up and returns early ([ModuleNode.py#L3449](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/997aeea7410c0b7e0904efab62553145064f2ff8/Cython/Compiler/ModuleNode.py#L3449-L3454)), so the new state is never filled.

After that, every module state lookup returns NULL. The `Py_mod_create` docs say it should return a new module object ([module.rst#L311-L314](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/4489dc3e16abb09aa2e50a4909ed33f2327ae77d/Doc/c-api/module.rst#L311-L314)).

No crash without module state, or with `CYTHON_PEP489_MULTI_PHASE_INIT=0`.

Found through asyncpg 0.31+ (MagicStack/asyncpg#1292), where coverage.py and Temporal's sandbox re-import it.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```cython
# demo.pyx
cdef class Base:
    pass

cdef class Child(Base):
    def __init__(self):
        Base.__init__(self)

def make():
    return Child()
```

```python
# setup.py
from Cython.Build import cythonize
from setuptools import Extension, setup

setup(
    ext_modules=cythonize(
        [Extension("demo", ["demo.pyx"], define_macros=[("CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE", "1")])],
        language_level=3,
    )
)
```

```python
# run.py
import sys

import demo

print(type(demo.make()).__name__, flush=True)
del sys.modules["demo"]
import demo

print(type(demo.make()).__name__, flush=True)
```

```
$ python setup.py build_ext --inplace && python -X faulthandler run.py
Child
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

Current thread 0x00000001f856dd80 (most recent call first):
  File ".../run.py", line 9 in <module>
```

Without the define it prints `Child` twice.

### Expected behaviour

The second import raises, and the first one keeps working. This change does that for me:

```diff
-    if (${module_cname})
+    if (${module_cname}) {
+    #if CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE
+        // CPython resets md_state of the module that Py_mod_create returns,
+        // so handing back the live module would wipe its state.
+        PyErr_Format(PyExc_ImportError,
+            "Module '%s' has already been imported into this interpreter. Re-importing it is not supported.",
+            def->m_name);
+        return NULL;
+    #else
         return __Pyx_NewRef(${module_cname});
+    #endif
+    }
```

With it, the repro raises `ImportError` and the first `demo.make()` still works. asyncpg built against it raises the same `ImportError`, and its subinterpreter tests still pass. Happy to open a PR with a `tests/run` test if this is the right direction.

### OS

macOS 26, arm64

### Python version

3.12.13 (also 3.13.13, 3.14.6)

### Cython version

3.3.0 and master 997aeea74

comment_data.body:
> The Py_mod_create docs say it should return a new module object 

That implies that the newref path is always wrong even without module state and mostly works by luck.

It's a bit of a shame that it has to fail completely. One of the nice things about (the idea of) module state is that it probably should be possible for it to import it multiple times. I think with the current lookup code that certainly isn't possible.

title: [BUG] Second import of a module built with CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE crashes
